title: Lecture 4.2: Writing the Conceptual Framework
text:
“Handwaving”
Handwaving is a term that describes a step that may be plausible but is not established by the stated argument
The authorization model can support
higher compliance cost→possible authorization loss
\text{higher compliance cost}
\rightarrow
\text{possible authorization loss}

It does not by itself establish
authorization loss→food access change→diet or health change
\text{authorization loss}
\rightarrow
\text{food access change}
\rightarrow
\text{diet or health change}

That downstream pathway requires relationships and evidence about inventory availability purchases and health.

Handwaving does not mean the conclusion is impossible. It means that the premises and intermediate steps presented so far do not establish it. In this example the omitted steps include whether households used an affected retailer whether alternative retailers replace that access and whether purchases respond.
[Sources] - Cheng (2004/Sources)

title: Lecture 4.2: Writing the Conceptual Framework
text:
SNAP example: in paragraph form

The revised standard may raise the cost of continued SNAP authorization, with the increase varying across retailers. Let BiB_i denote the benefit a retailer receives from authorization, including SNAP-related sales, and let Ki(r)K_i(r) denote the compliance cost. Holding BiB_i fixed, the model predicts an authorization loss when Ki(r)K_i(r) exceeds BiB_i. This prediction motivates an analysis of authorization changes by store type and local SNAP participation. The available data do not establish changes in inventory, household access, purchases, diet, or health.

title: Lecture 5.2: Data Collection via APIs
text:
Example 1: land use
Question
Which crop and land-cover classes does the Cropland Data Layer assign in Larimer County in 2024?
Source
USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer through the CropScape service
Observation
Each raster cell has a modeled crop or land-cover class for a particular year
CropScape documentation | CropScapeR documentation

title: Lecture 5.2: Data Collection via APIs
section: Request a Cropland Data Layer map
text:
Request a Cropland Data Layer map
library(CropScapeR)

larimer_cdl <- GetCDLData(
  aoi = "08069",
  year = 2024,
  type = "f",
  save_path = "data/raw/cdl_larimer_2024.tif"
)

raster::plot(larimer_cdl)
08069 is the five-digit Census code for Larimer County
The saved GeoTIFF contains a grid of land-cover codes and the information needed to locate those cells on a map

section: Use and assess the land-use data
text:
Use and assess the land-use data
Possible uses

Map crop locations
Calculate acreage by crop class
Compare annual crop patterns
Define land-use exposure near water infrastructure or development

Checks

Crop-class definitions for each year
Classification accuracy for the study region and crop
Pixel resolution and coordinate system
Treatment of double cropping and small fields
Consistency of the study boundary across years

The CDL records modeled land-cover classes. Parcel ownership, zoning, and management practices require additional sources

title: Lecture 5.2: Data Collection via APIs
text:
Example 2: water
Question
What was the daily flow of the Cache la Poudre River during the 2024 growing season?
Source
USGS Water Data API
Observation
Each row reports a daily statistic for one parameter at one monitoring location
USGS monitoring location 06752260 | dataRetrieval tutorial

title: Lecture 5.2: Data Collection via APIs
text:
Request daily streamflow
library(dataRetrieval)

poudre_flow <- read_waterdata_daily(
  monitoring_location_id = "USGS-06752260",
  parameter_code = "00060",
  time = c("2024-04-01", "2024-09-30")
)

names(poudre_flow)
head(poudre_flow)
00060 is the USGS parameter code for discharge
The returned columns include date, value, unit, approval status, qualifiers, station geometry, and a time-series identifier

title: Lecture 5.2: Data Collection via APIs
text:
Plot and summarize streamflow
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(poudre_flow, aes(x = time, y = value)) +
  geom_line(color = "#245a81") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Daily discharge",
    title = "Cache la Poudre River at Fort Collins"
  )
The daily records can also be summarized as

Growing-season mean or median flow
Number of days below a selected threshold
Timing of peak flow
Deviations from a historical seasonal pattern

Read the unit attached to each series
Examine provisional and approved status
Identify missing dates and changes in the operating record
Learn whether reservoirs, diversions, or return flows affect the gauge
Define the geographic relationship between the gauge and the study area

The gauge measures conditions at one point on a river network. A study of irrigation access may also require diversion service areas, water rights, or delivery records

fort_collins_weather <- get_power(
  community = "AG",
  lonlat = c(-105.08, 40.58),
  pars = c("T2M_MAX", "T2M_MIN", "PRECTOTCORR"),
  temporal_api = "daily",
  dates = c("2024-04-01", "2024-09-30")

head(fort_collins_weather)

The three requested measures are maximum temperature, minimum temperature, and precipitation

Request a free key from the Census API key page
Open the user-level environment file from R

library(tidycensus)

larimer_income <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = c(median_income = "B19013_001"),
  state = "CO",
  county = "Larimer",
  year = 2024,
  survey = "acs5",
  geometry = TRUE,

head(larimer_income)
